title: This Songbird Hangs Its Dinner on Barbed Wire, and It's Not Just Storing It
subject: loggerhead shrike

scenes.text: A songbird hangs its dinner on barbed wire. There's a reason it waits.
The loggerhead shrike is robin-sized, but it hunts lizards, small mammals and other birds.
Its feet are weak, so it can't pin prey down to tear it. It spears the meal on a thorn instead.
Some prey is toxic. Lubber grasshoppers can make animals gag, vomit, even die.
So the shrike hangs them up. After a day or two, the toxins break down.
It's curing its food, like olives. To the shrike, barbed wire is a pantry.

description:
The loggerhead shrike impales prey on thorns and barbed wire.
Its feet are weak, so the thorn holds the meal while its beak tears it apart. Biologists also think hanging toxic grasshoppers for a day or two lets the toxins break down, a bit like curing olives.
What other animal has a pantry like this?
first_comment: Shrikes are nicknamed butcher birds. Would you have guessed a songbird could hunt another bird?
